title: A novel RANKL-targeted flavonoid glycoside prevents osteoporosis through inhibiting NFATc1 and reactive oxygen species.
authors: Hong, Guoju; Chen, Zhenqiu; Han, Xiaorui; Zhou, Lin; Pang, Fengxiang; Wu, Rishana; Shen, Yingshan; He, Xiaoming; Hong, Zhinan; Li, Ziqi; He, Wei; Wei, Qiushi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮苷Rob通过靶向RANKL抑制破骨细胞防治骨质疏松，仅涉及蛋白-配体对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Osteoporosis is characterized by excessive bone resorption due to enhanced osteoclast activation. Stimulation of nuclear factor of activated T cells 1 (NFATc1) and accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) are important mechanisms underlying osteoclastogenesis. Robinin (Rob) is a flavonoid glycoside that has shown anti-inflammatory and antioxidative effects in previous studies, but little is known about its effects on bone homeostasis. The purpose of our research was to investigate whether Rob could prevent bone resorption in ovariectomized (OVX) mice by suppressing osteoclast production through its underlying mechanisms. METHODS: The docking pose of Rob and RANKL was identified by protein-ligand molecular docking. Rob was added to bone marrow macrophages (BMMs) stimulated by nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) ligand (RANKL). The effects of Rob on osteoclastic activity were evaluated by positive tartrate resistant acid phosphatase (TRAcP) staining kit and hydroxyapatite resorption assay. RANKL-induced ROS generation in osteoclasts was detected by H(2) DCFDA and MitoSox Red staining. The classic molecular cascades triggered by RANKL, such as NF-kappaB, ROS, calcium oscillations, and NFATc1-mediated signaling pathways, were investigated using Fluo4 staining, western blot, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. In addition, an OVX mouse model mimicking estrogen-deficient osteoporosis was created to evaluate the therapeutic effects of Rob in vivo. RESULTS: Computational docking results showed that Rob could bind specifically to RANKL's predicted binding sites. In vitro, Rob inhibited RANKL-mediated osteoclastogenesis dose-dependently without obvious cytotoxicity at low concentrations. We also found that Rob attenuated RANKL-induced mitochondrial ROS production or enhanced activities of ROS-scavenging enzymes, and ultimately reduced intracellular ROS levels. Rob abrogated the RANKL-induced mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and NF-kappaB signaling pathways, and subsequently blocked NFATc1 signaling and TRAcP expression. In addition, Rob inhibited osteoclast proliferation by downregulating the expression of osteoclast target genes (Acp5, Cathepsin K, Atp6v0d2, Nfact1, c-Fos, and Mmp9) and reducing Ca(2+) oscillations. Our in vivo results showed that Rob reduced bone resorption in OVX animal model by repressing osteoclast activity and function. CONCLUSIONS: Rob inhibits the activation of osteoclasts by targeting RANKL and is therefore a potential osteoporosis drug.
abstract_zh: 背景与目的：骨质疏松症的特征是由于破骨细胞活化增强而导致的骨吸收过度。活化T细胞核因子1（NFATc1）的刺激和活性氧（ROS）的积累是破骨细胞生成的重要机制。罗宾苷（Rob）是一种黄酮苷，在以往研究中显示出抗炎和抗氧化作用，但对其在骨稳态中的影响知之甚少。本研究旨在探讨Rob是否通过其潜在机制抑制破骨细胞生成，从而预防去卵巢（OVX）小鼠的骨吸收。方法：通过蛋白质-配体分子对接确定Rob与RANKL的对接姿态。将Rob添加到受核因子-κB（NF-κB）配体（RANKL）刺激的骨髓巨噬细胞（BMMs）中。通过阳性抗酒石酸酸性磷酸酶（TRAcP）染色试剂盒和羟基磷灰石吸收实验评估Rob对破骨细胞活性的影响。通过H(2)DCFDA和MitoSox Red染色检测RANKL诱导的破骨细胞中ROS生成。使用Fluo4染色、蛋白质印迹和定量实时聚合酶链反应研究RANKL触发的经典分子级联反应，如NF-κB、ROS、钙振荡和NFATc1介导的信号通路。此外，建立模拟雌激素缺乏性骨质疏松症的OVX小鼠模型，以评估Rob在体内的治疗效果。结果：计算对接结果显示，Rob能特异性结合RANKL的预测结合位点。在体外，Rob以剂量依赖性方式抑制RANKL介导的破骨细胞生成，且在低浓度下无明显细胞毒性。我们还发现，Rob减弱了RANKL诱导的线粒体ROS产生或增强了ROS清除酶的活性，最终降低了细胞内ROS水平。Rob阻断了RANKL诱导的丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）和NF-κB信号通路，并随后抑制了NFATc1信号和TRAcP表达。此外，Rob通过下调破骨细胞靶基因（Acp5、Cathepsin K、Atp6v0d2、Nfact1、c-Fos和Mmp9）的表达并减少Ca(2+)振荡来抑制破骨细胞增殖。我们的体内结果显示，Rob通过抑制破骨细胞活性和功能，减少了OVX动物模型中的骨吸收。结论：Rob通过靶向RANKL抑制破骨细胞活化，因此是一种潜在的骨质疏松症药物。
